prompt: Economic development in the countryside has improved the quality of life in urban areas more than in the countryside. This creates a gap. What problems does this cause, and how might these problems be reduced?
essay: In contemporary society, the development of economy in nations has improved the quality of life in urban areas more than in the rural areas. This could raise issue in the overall development of the country and reduce the economy; however, this can be solved by allocating massive reserves and utilising the technological advancements to improve the standard of living in the countryside. This essay will discuss the reasons that creates the gap and provide viable solutions to mitigate it. The primary catalyst of this rising issue is due to political and educational deficiencies. Many individuals living in villages remain unaware of the governance system and their constitutional rights. Additionally, due to widespread financial instability, parents often cannot afford to educate their children. The funds provided by the government are frequently insufficient to build the infrastructure necessary for quality education and improvement. For instance, a recent survey conducted in India revealed that a significant number of rural children do not attend schools regularly due to poor infrastructure and poverty. As a result, these citizens remain excluded from official welfare schemes and legal protections. To mitigate this growing problem, the government must enforce strict rules and regulations on the officials to fulfil the allotted work. Additionally, by providing huge finances to build modern school facilities, integrate technology, upgrade healthcare systems and construct better transport networks, the standard of living of can be enhanced. Monthly awareness campaigns regarding healthcare, financial literacy, and education are essential. Consequently, improving rural lives will directly boost a nation’s overall economy and progression. In conclusion, although there is a severe gap between the rural and urban areas due to less funds and unawareness, this can be resolved. By implementing awareness campaigns, allocating massive capital and improving the infrastructure, governments can successfully bridge this divide and ensure balanced national growth.
